cases.customer_question: Are compliance folders required even when an OEM product already has Bluetooth qualification?
cases.actual_issue: The customer assumed compliance-folder requirements might only apply when the original product lacked Bluetooth qualification. The thread clarifies that compliance-folder obligations apply more broadly under updated qualification rules.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Even if a Bluetooth product was already qualified by another company, documentation still needs to be retained. The requirement is tied to the qualification program rules rather than whether the original product was certified.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that qualification program changes effective from July 2024 require maintenance of a compliance folder even for OEM-based qualification scenarios. The required documentation may include materials similar to those used in radio certification activities, such as manuals, block diagrams, product drawings, and antenna information.
cases.decision_logic: Compliance-folder obligations are independent of whether the original Bluetooth implementation was previously qualified. Documentation retention is now a separate qualification requirement.
cases.final_recommendation: Prepare and retain a compliance folder containing the required qualification evidence and supporting technical documentation regardless of whether the product is an OEM-derived design.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: The company may fail an audit or be unable to demonstrate qualification compliance because required supporting documentation was not maintained.
